name: OpenShell valid OCSF policy denial
description: Detects structurally valid OCSF network-policy denial evidence from an OpenShell sandbox.
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: Expected policy validation or approved negative testing
note: Triage the sandbox, gateway, policy version, destination, agent trace/request identifiers, and surrounding lifecycle evidence. Confirm whether the denial was expected before escalating.
setup: Requires the OpenShell CloudEvents-to-ECS contract, mapping version 1, and the logs-openshell.security-*-v1 index namespace. Confirm event.original is redacted before analyst access. Create or update this rule only with the dedicated openshell_detection_service identity; never attach an OpenShell policy-write credential or automatic policy response. This event-level rule schedules on downstream event.ingested so delayed persistent-queue delivery remains detectable; @timestamp remains the source event time for investigation.

name: OpenShell repeated policy denials by sandbox
description: Escalates three or more structurally valid OCSF network-policy denials from the same gateway, workspace, and sandbox within the five-minute detection window.
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: Approved repeated negative testing or a known misconfigured agent workflow
note: Treat repeated denied actions as higher priority than an isolated denial. Confirm the grouped gateway, workspace, and sandbox in kibana.alert.threshold_result, inspect distinct source event IDs and destinations, correlate agent trace/session context, and determine whether the agent is retrying or probing policy boundaries.

name: OpenShell agent trace correlation gap
description: Detects Relay spans that could not be completely bound to both an OpenShell sandbox and agent session.
false_positives: Expected partial context from a validated Relay instrumentation limitation
note: Treat missing sandbox or session context as an observability integrity issue. Inspect openshell.correlation.missing and invalid, then reconcile the affected gateway and time window without claiming causal attribution.

name: OpenShell agent activity followed by policy denial
description: Detects privacy-filtered root agent execution followed by a real OpenShell policy denial for the same sandbox within five minutes.
query: sequence by openshell.sandbox.id with maxspan=5m [any where event.dataset == "openshell.agent" and event.action == "agent"] [any where event.dataset == "openshell.security" and tags == "policy-denial"]
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: Expected policy-negative testing or an approved agent task that intentionally exercises a denied destination
note: This alert proves temporal sequence, not causal intent. Confirm the same gateway, workspace, sandbox, session/trace context, policy version, destination, and exact evidence times. Preserve the redacted CloudEvent and privacy-filtered trace identifiers before escalation; never infer prompt or tool content that was intentionally removed.
setup: Requires both versioned OpenShell ECS lanes, the post-privacy Relay OTLP contract, and the policy-denial tag invariant (only structurally valid OCSF class 4001 denial evidence receives that tag). Create or update this rule only with the dedicated openshell_detection_service identity; never attach an OpenShell policy-write credential or automatic policy response.

name: OpenShell sandbox probed multiple denied destinations
description: Detects one sandbox producing three or more valid policy denials against three or more distinct destinations within five minutes.
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: Approved negative testing, endpoint discovery tests, or a misconfigured workload iterating over expected service endpoints
note: Scope the alert to its gateway, workspace, sandbox, and source-time window. Confirm distinct destination addresses and ports, preserve every evidence ID, compare requested endpoints with the approved task and policy version, then inspect nearby agent stages and source-gap evidence. This indicates repeated boundary interaction; it does not prove malicious intent.
setup: Requires structurally valid OpenShell OCSF policy-denial evidence with destination.address promoted by the Elastic integration. Create or update this rule only with the dedicated openshell_detection_service identity; never attach an OpenShell policy-write credential or automatic policy response.

name: OpenShell policy change followed by denied action
description: Detects exported policy-change evidence followed by a valid policy denial for the same sandbox within fifteen minutes.
query: sequence by openshell.sandbox.id with maxspan=15m [any where event.dataset == "openshell.security" and tags == "policy-change"] [any where event.dataset == "openshell.security" and tags == "policy-denial" and openshell.validation.status == "valid"]
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: An approved policy rollout that intentionally tightens access and immediately exercises the new boundary
note: Verify change authorization, policy version and revision, direct policy-chunk identifiers, and the exact source-time sequence. Compare the denied destination or operation with the intended policy change. This is temporal context, not proof that the change caused the denial; the exporter never mutates policy.
setup: Requires exported read-only policy evidence and structurally valid policy-denial evidence in the OpenShell security lane. Create or update this rule only with the dedicated openshell_detection_service identity; never attach an OpenShell policy-write credential or automatic policy response.

name: OpenShell policy denial followed by evidence source gap
description: Detects a valid policy denial followed by an observable source-gap warning for the same sandbox within five minutes.
query: sequence by openshell.sandbox.id with maxspan=5m [any where event.dataset == "openshell.security" and tags == "policy-denial" and openshell.validation.status == "valid"] [any where event.dataset == "openshell.security" and tags == "source-gap"]
author: NVIDIA OpenShell Event Exporter reference
false_positives: A sandbox intentionally stopped immediately after a known negative test, with complete durable OCSF reconciliation for the affected interval
note: Treat the interval as potentially incomplete. Preserve denial and gap evidence IDs, bound the last known good and first recovered timestamps, check durable OCSF file coordinates and exporter queues, and reconcile gateway lifecycle state. Do not infer inactivity or safety from missing stream records.
setup: Requires policy-denial and source-gap tag invariants in the OpenShell security lane. Create or update this rule only with the dedicated openshell_detection_service identity; never attach an OpenShell policy-write credential or automatic policy response.
